interpretations.GG: Wild-type (C/C). Standard MTHFR enzyme activity and folate metabolism.
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous (C/T). ~30-40% reduction in MTHFR enzyme efficiency. Mildly reduced folate conversion.
interpretations.AA: Homozygous risk (T/T). ~60-70% reduction in MTHFR enzyme activity. Homocysteine levels may rise; high-potency methylfolate supplementation is often recommended.

interpretations.TT: Wild-type (A/A). Standard MTHFR activity and BH4 synthesis.
interpretations.TG: Heterozygous (A/C). ~20% reduction in enzyme activity. Minimal impact on its own, but combined with C677T (compound heterozygosity), it reduces efficiency to ~45-50%.
interpretations.GG: Homozygous risk (C/C). ~40% reduction in enzyme activity. Can affect BH4 levels, impacting dopamine, serotonin, and nitric oxide synthesis.
Homozygous Val/Val ('Warrior'). Rapid dopamine clearance. High stress tolerance and emotional resilience, but may require more stimulation for peak focus.
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous Val/Met ('Balanced'). Intermediate dopamine clearance. A balanced profile combining cognitive flexibility with moderate stress tolerance.
interpretations.AA: Homozygous Met/Met ('Worrier'). Slow dopamine clearance. High baseline dopamine levels, leading to superior memory, focus, and executive function, but lower threshold for stress overload.

interpretations.GG: A2/A2 (Homozygous Wild-type). Standard density of dopamine D2 receptors. Baseline reward pathways operate normally.
interpretations.AG: A1/A2 (Heterozygous). ~30% reduction in dopamine D2 receptor density. Linked to a higher drive for reward, novelty seeking, and susceptibility to habit formation.
interpretations.AA: A1/A1 (Homozygous Risk). ~40% reduction in dopamine D2 receptor density. High susceptibility to dopamine-seeking behaviors, reward deficiency syndrome, and habit forming.

interpretations.GG: Val/Val (Wild-type). Standard secretion of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor. Optimized for active neuroplasticity, memory formation, and synaptic growth.
interpretations.AG: Val/Met (Heterozygous). Moderately reduced activity-dependent BDNF secretion. Balances memory retention dynamics with resilience under acute emotional strain.
interpretations.AA: Met/Met (Homozygous Risk). ~30% reduction in activity-dependent BDNF secretion. Associated with altered working memory and slower cognitive processing, but sometimes linked to unique creative thinking and focus profiles.

interpretations.GG: Wild-type (C/C). Standard circadian rhythm. Morning-leaning chronotype, associated with easier early waking and stable sleep latency.
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous (C/G). Intermediate chronotype. Adaptable sleep schedule with balanced morning/night energy levels.
interpretations.AA: Homozygous Risk (G/G). Night owl chronotype. Associated with delayed sleep phase, higher late-evening alertness, and susceptibility to sleep debt in standard schedules.
Wild-type. Standard expression of Acetylserotonin O-methyltransferase. Optimized conversion of serotonin to melatonin for normal sleep cycles.
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous. Intermediate ASMT activity. Melatonin production is generally stable, but sleep onset may be more sensitive to evening blue light exposure.
interpretations.GG: Homozygous Risk. Reduced ASMT activity. Slower melatonin synthesis, leading to delayed sleep onset and potential sleep quality issues under artificial evening light.
Lactose Intolerant (C/C). Adult lactase non-persistence. The body naturally winds down lactase enzyme production in adulthood, leading to digestive sensitivity to dairy.
interpretations.AG: Lactose Tolerant (C/T). Lactase persistence. A single copy of the persistence allele keeps lactase active, enabling normal dairy digestion into adulthood.
interpretations.AA: Lactose Tolerant (T/T). Homozygous lactase persistence. Optimized for dairy digestion into adulthood with standard lactase levels.

interpretations.CC: Homozygous R/R (Sprint/Power). Full presence of alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch fibers. Optimized for explosive sprint, power, and muscle force production.
interpretations.TC: Heterozygous R/X (Mixed/Balanced). Moderate alpha-actinin-3 levels. A hybrid profile showing balanced capacity for both speed-power and long-distance endurance.
interpretations.TT: Homozygous X/X (Endurance). Complete lack of alpha-actinin-3. Fast-twitch fibers act more like slow-twitch fibers, yielding exceptional muscular efficiency, recovery, and long-distance aerobic endurance.

interpretations.GG: Homozygous Wild-type. Efficient conversion of plant-based omega-3s (ALA) into active long-chain fatty acids (EPA and DHA).
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous. Intermediate omega-3 conversion efficiency. Benefits from dietary intake of pre-formed EPA/DHA (e.g. wild fish or algal oil) to maintain optimal brain and joint health.
interpretations.AA: Homozygous Risk. Poor conversion of plant-based ALA (flax/chia) to EPA/DHA. Direct supplementation of active marine-source EPA/DHA is highly recommended.

interpretations.GG: Homozygous Wild-type. Efficient conversion of plant beta-carotene into active Vitamin A (retinol).
interpretations.GT: Heterozygous. ~30% reduction in beta-carotene conversion. Plant-source carotenes should be supplemented with direct Vitamin A sources (retinyl palmitate, cod liver oil, eggs/dairy).
interpretations.TT: Homozygous Risk. ~60-70% reduction in plant beta-carotene conversion. Relying only on carrots/leafy greens for Vitamin A is insufficient; direct active Vitamin A (retinol) is highly recommended.

interpretations.AA: A/A (Wild-type). Standard mu-opioid receptor density and sensitivity. Standard pain tolerance and beta-endorphin signaling.
interpretations.AG: A/G (Heterozygous). Moderately reduced mu-opioid receptor binding. Associated with slightly higher pain sensitivity, altered response to opioid medication, and a unique reward pathway threshold.
interpretations.GG: G/G (Homozygous Risk). ~3-fold reduction in mu-opioid receptor expression. Associated with significantly higher sensitivity to physical and social pain, and requiring higher doses of pain medication.
G/G (Homozygous Wild-type). Standard oxytocin receptor density. High stress resilience, social connection, and intuitive empathy readings.
interpretations.AG: G/A (Heterozygous). Intermediate oxytocin sensitivity. Balanced empathy traits and moderate stress resilience under social pressure.
interpretations.AA: A/A (Homozygous Risk). Reduced oxytocin receptor density. Associated with lower baseline social stress tolerance, unique social communication styles, and a tendency to process empathy cognitively rather than raw affectively.

interpretations.GG: Homozygous Wild-type. Wet earwax and standard underarm apocrine gland secretion. Normal body odor profile.
interpretations.AG: Heterozygous. Wet earwax and standard apocrine gland secretion. Normal body odor profile.
interpretations.AA: Homozygous Mutation. Dry earwax and a complete absence of the chemical compound (trimethylamine/fatty acids) that underarm bacteria feed on. Zero underarm body odor; deodorant is biologically unnecessary.

interpretations.GG: Non-taster (AVI/AVI). Insensitive to bitter compounds like PTC/PROP. Broccoli, kale, dark chocolate, and black coffee taste mild or pleasant.
interpretations.CG: Medium Taster (PAV/AVI). Moderate sensitivity to bitter compounds. Can detect bitterness in cruciferous vegetables but finds them tolerable.
interpretations.CC: Supertaster (PAV/PAV). Extreme sensitivity to bitter taste compounds. Cruciferous vegetables, cilantro, and dark IPAs can taste overwhelmingly bitter.

interpretations.AA: Fast Caffeine Metabolizer. Caffeine is cleared rapidly by the liver. Coffee provides clean, short-acting focus without lingering cardiovascular stress or sleep disturbance.
interpretations.AC: Slow Caffeine Metabolizer. Caffeine clears slowly. Prolonged effects, higher risk of jitteriness, and potential sleep disruption if consumed in the afternoon.
interpretations.CC: Ultra-Slow Caffeine Metabolizer. Caffeine remains in the bloodstream for a very long duration. Increased cardiovascular risk under high daily caffeine intake; afternoon coffee significantly compromises sleep.
Wild-type. Standard melanocortin 1 receptor function. Normal hair pigment, standard pain thresholds, and baseline general anesthesia sensitivity.
interpretations.CT: Heterozygous. Single copy carrier of red hair variant. Subtle variations in skin sensitivity; normal anesthesia sensitivity.
interpretations.TT: Homozygous Red Hair variant. Low MC1R activity, yielding red hair, fair skin/freckles. Biologically linked to higher sensitivity to cold/heat pain, higher tolerance to electrical pain, and requiring ~20% more general anesthesia in clinical procedures.
